original.closure_text: Case Closed. Closed date : 2018-05-30 08:54:17.5 Case Resolved Dear Constituent     When utility companies dig into a street they obviously disturb the soil underneath the roadway    In some cases excavations can go down up to 10 feet.     Cities and Towns expect that there will be some settlement after the backfilling has been completed    That is why in Boston all backfilled paved excavations are considered temporary    After a certain period of time  the temporary repair is then permanently repaired    The Boston Public Works Construction Inspection Unit (CIU) will identify temporary patches that are not smooth and level and have the utility or private contractor repair them     We do not expect temporary patches to look as good as permanent patches.     However we do definitively make utilities and private contractors do over temporary patches until the permanent repair can be done.     As far as the active Dorchester Ave patch work is concerned the inspectors are stating that the temporary patches are acceptable until the permanent repairs are done    For any questions or concerns  please contact the number listed below    Sincerely       Mark Cardarelli  Supervisor of Utility Coordination and Compliance  Boston Public Works Department  [removed] Office

original.closure_text: Case Closed. Closed date : 2018-08-06 11:26:38.91 Case Noted Dear Constituent      Thank you for your comments regarding roadway safety on L Street in South Boston.  Your correspondence has been forwarded to the attention of the Boston Transportation Department for review.     Over the next several weeks  the City of Boston’s Transportation and Public Works Departments will be working with the South Boston community to identify and implement changes aimed at improving roadway safety along L Street.  The City has started making short-term investments to calm speeds and improve intersections  and these will continue through the fall.  Long-term advancements will focus on additional upgrades to L Street as well as the larger City Point neighborhood of South Boston.     An initial inspection of the intersection showed traffic-related pavement markings and signage in the vicinity of L Street and East 6th Street to be in good condition.  Although speed was determined not to have been a factor in the recent crash at the intersection of L Street and East 6th Street  the City has installed a speed radar sign on L Street inbound at the approach to East 6thStreet to further remind drivers to drive slowly and proceed with caution in this dense residential neighborhood.  A speed radar sign on L Street outbound  also at the approach to East 6th Street  will be installed shortly.  In addition  yield lines will soon be painted on L Street at both approaches to East 6th Street to supplement the existing pedestrian crosswalks.     Mayor Walsh and BTD have long been committed to improving safety on L Street and the surrounding vicinity.  Updated traffic counts are currently being taken on L Street and they will be used to inform a long term plan.     Safety for all users of Boston’s streets has always been  and will continue to be  the first priority of the Boston Transportation Department.  Significant work is accomplished every day by BTD and the Public Works Department to ensure roadway safety in South Boston and every other neighborhood in the City and this effort will persist.  Safe  reliable and equitable travel on Boston’s streets is our goal.     Thank you for your concern.
